chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahzar, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from al-Arzami, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in the Hajar, sitting under the gutter. A man was disputing with another man, and one of them said to his companion: 'By Allah, you do not know from where the wind blows?' When he insisted, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Do you know from where the wind blows?' He said: 'No, but I hear people saying so.' I then said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'From where does the wind blow? I am your ransom.'

He said: 'Indeed, the wind is imprisoned beneath this Eastern Corner (Rukn ash-Shami). When Allah, Exalted and Glorious, wills to send forth some of it, He releases it. As for the south wind, it is the south wind; as for the north wind, it is the north wind; as for the east wind (Saba), it is the east wind; as for the west wind (Dubar), it is the west wind.' Then he said: 'And the sign of that is that you will always see this Corner moving in winter and summer, night and day continuously.'

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ الشَّامِي: The Eastern Corner of the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: Where are the winds stored according to Shia hadith, and what is the sign of their release?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the cosmological mechanism of wind distribution, correcting popular ignorance by attributing its source to a specific, imprisoned location beneath the Eastern Corner (al-Rukn al-Shami) of the Kaaba. This account highlights the Imam's role in revealing hidden natural signs (*ayat*) and demonstrates the integration of physical observation—such as the corner's perpetual movement—with divine will, reinforcing the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Kaaba as a central axis of cosmic order.

en.basel-kadem: 15. We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, from Hasan bin Mahbub, from Ali bin Ri’ab, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And whatever afflicts you of a calamity, it is due to what your hands have acquired, and He pardons much.» [42:30] Have you seen that which afflicted Ali and his Household, was it due to what their hands acquired, while they are a Household of Purity and are Infallible?

He said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, used to repent to Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and seek forgiveness from Him every day day and night a hundred times without a sin. Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, specifies His Allies with calamities in order that He might reward them for them without (them having committed) a sin.
